About me

I'm Roy Segal. I work on machine learning for brain signals, video and physical systems.

I start with the data and the problem: which representations are useful, how to evaluate a model, and what it takes to make it work in practice. My work spans multimodal learning, computer vision and scientific forecasting.

EEG foundation models

I'm currently developing foundation models for EEG at brain.space, learning representations of brain activity that can support different downstream tasks.

Multimodal AI · Video + Language

Video-to-text and real-time computer vision

I implemented and fine-tuned multimodal video-to-text transformers. Our video-content analysis reached a 78% similarity score; our instance-segmentation work for real-time vision achieved error rates below 10%.

This work also involved keeping up with state-of-the-art models, evaluating new approaches and adapting them to our data and deployment constraints.

Kaggle · 19th of 1,412 teams

Mouse behavior recognition

With Amit Aharoni, I built a solution for the MABe Challenge that recognizes individual and social actions from mouse tracking data. We combined invariant body-keypoint features with WaveNet and GRU models to handle missing measurements and noisy labels.

Our Kaggle solution ↗

Kaggle · 19th of 638 teams · Silver medal

AI model runtime prediction

With Amit Aharoni, I used graph neural networks to rank compiler configurations by model runtime. We repeatedly injected configuration embeddings through residual connections so that this signal remained visible in large computational graphs.
